connectivity.body: PeeringDB’s measure of interconnection facilities or coverage fell materially to a floor of 250. Other public records list 168 active U.S. internet exchange points with 2,805 combined reported members, as well as 90 U.S. international submarine cable systems. Because the declining figure is a coverage floor, it should not be treated by itself as proof that physical network capacity fell. These counts establish the footprint’s scale, but not the bandwidth or redundancy available in any particular data-center market.
connectivity.headline: The interconnection coverage measure falls within a broad U.S. network footprint

macro.body: Technology investment and production remain strong. Information-processing investment is growing 16.8%, while semiconductor and electronic-component output is growing 19.9%. Public-market readings have also improved: the AI Equity Index rose materially to 31.9, the median one-year return reached 13.0%, and 63.2% of covered companies have positive one-year returns. Barron’s report that TSMC shares fell after blowout earnings is a company-specific exception to that firmer aggregate picture. Credit markets present a less favorable picture. Reported private-equity funds held $8.523 trillion in Form PF net assets at the end of 2025, but this is not liquid cash or a measure of AI financing capacity. Reuters reported that AI credit concerns drove default insurance for U.S. technology debt to record highs, and the Financial Times reported selling in data-center bonds. A large private-capital base can therefore coexist with debt markets that penalize individual AI-infrastructure borrowers. Physical delivery has a similar distinction between scale and readiness. Available project records list 1,556 data-center sites in development against 3,068 operating sites, equivalent to 0.51 development site per operating site; a separate tracker follows 894 active-pipeline sites. The active power interconnection queue totals 2,061 GW, yet only 24.2% is in executed-agreement or construction stages, and 13% of the 2000–2020 cohort reached operation. The site and queue datasets cover different project universes, but both caution against treating pipeline size as delivered capacity.
macro.headline: Investment signals strengthen while credit and infrastructure execution remain uneven

power.body: Commercial electricity demand is growing 3.1%, versus 1.2% for total retail demand, while retail prices are up 4.4%. Net planned generation additions total 225.2 GW through the pipeline horizon. Utility Dive reported that MISO proposed a fast-track study process for large loads and generation. The proposal concerns study timing; it does not establish when planned capacity will connect or how local supply-demand balances will change.
power.headline: Commercial demand leads electricity growth as faster grid studies are proposed

editorial_briefing.style_reference: AI Macro is a research platform that examines the development of the U.S. AI economy from capital investment and physical construction through deployment, adoption, and economic results. It uses publicly available data to relate corporate and market activity to the physical systems required to support the buildout. It evaluates the extent to which that investment produces durable economic value and how its effects are transmitted through the broader U.S. economy.

body.text: PeeringDB’s interconnection-facility or coverage-floor measure increased materially to 1,378. The broader recorded footprint includes 168 active U.S. internet exchange points with 2,805 combined reported members and 90 U.S. international submarine cable systems. The higher figure materially expands the measured network footprint, but these counts do not show bandwidth, redundancy, or capacity available in a specific data-center market.

headline.text: Network coverage rises materially, without a matching measure of capacity

body.text: Commercial electricity demand is growing 3.1%, ahead of 1.2% growth in total retail demand, while retail prices are up 4.4%. Net planned generation additions total 225.2 GW, but this is pipeline capacity rather than delivered supply. Utility Dive also reported on Google’s virtual power plant in PJM. That introduces a different type of grid project into the power picture, although the report does not establish its scale or effect on PJM’s supply-demand balance.

headline.text: Commercial demand leads electricity growth while Utility Dive reports on Google’s virtual power plant in PJM
Infrastructure measures are expanding, while power delivery and economic diffusion remain uneven

paragraphs.text: Hardware and infrastructure activity remains substantial. Semiconductor and electronic-component output is growing 19.9%, available project records list 1,556 data-center sites in development, and PeeringDB’s interconnection-facility or coverage-floor measure rose materially to 1,378. The last measure enlarges the observed network footprint, but it is not a measure of bandwidth or capacity available in a particular market.

Electricity shows a clear gap between planned scale and demonstrated availability. Commercial demand is growing 3.1%, compared with 1.2% total retail demand, and retail prices are up 4.4%. Net planned generation additions total 225.2 GW, but the active interconnection queue contains 2,061 GW, only 24.2% of which is in executed-agreement or construction stages; 13% of the 2000–2020 queue cohort reached operation. Utility Dive’s report on Google’s virtual power plant in PJM adds another type of grid response, but does not establish how materially the project changes the regional supply-demand balance.

Downstream use and economic effects remain mixed. Some generative-AI use is reported by 61.8% of adults ages 18–64, while 23.8% of businesses report current AI use and 27.7% expect to use it within six months. Nonfarm-business productivity is growing 2.2% and real output 2.5%, but those aggregate measures do not isolate AI’s contribution. Only one tracked AI-linked labor channel has positive employment growth, and the strongest—power and communication construction—is growing 0.8%. The evidence remains clearer for infrastructure investment than for broadly shared AI-driven gains.

diagnostics.text: Electricity shows a clear gap between planned scale and demonstrated availability. Commercial demand is growing 3.1%, compared with 1.2% total retail demand, and retail prices are up 4.4%. Net planned generation additions total 225.2 GW, but the active interconnection queue contains 2,061 GW, only 24.2% of which is in executed-agreement or construction stages; 13% of the 2000–2020 queue cohort reached operation. Utility Dive’s report on Google’s virtual power plant in PJM adds another type of grid response, but does not establish how materially the project changes the regional supply-demand balance.

editorial_synthesis.instructions:
You are writing the current research update for AI Macro.

Use only the findings and recent developments in the supplied briefing. Decide what matters, connect related evidence when the relationship is supported, and explain it in clear, natural English for an intelligent general reader. Prioritize significance over coverage. It is fine for the evidence to be mixed. Do not force unrelated facts into one story.

The style reference shows the desired level of restraint, specificity, and sentence construction. Match those qualities without copying its wording. Write like a careful human analyst. Use concrete subjects and verbs. Avoid rhetorical gimmicks and artificial-sounding transitions. Do not mention the prompt, the briefing, evidence IDs, validation, methodology, or the writing process.

On a normal update, candidate_domains identifies sections that may deserve replacement. Update only the domain Reads for which you can write something materially more useful than the prior publication; you may return no domain Reads when none deserves replacement. On a bootstrap publication, write every candidate domain because no prior Read exists. Always write one new Macro Read that explains the most important current story across the platform in two to four coherent paragraphs.

Do not inventory every supplied metric or news item. Use a number only when it helps the reader understand magnitude. Use recent developments when they materially sharpen the interpretation of the measured findings. Treat news reports as reported developments, not as proof of a broader causal claim.

Attach only the fact_ids and event_ids that actually support each passage. Those IDs are citations for the application and must never appear in the prose. Do not invent numbers, facts, events, causes, or forecasts.

Return only the structured response.
